strengths: WhisperX has excellent pt-BR support with word-level timestamps
Portuguese phonology is well-mapped to IPA/XSAMPA for viseme conversion
Nasal vowels (ã, õ, ẽ) have distinct acoustic signatures for reliable detection
Contractions (do=de+o, na=em+a) are handled well by modern ASR
Clitics (dizer-lhe) can be detected through prosodic boundaries
challenges: Vowel reduction in fast speech requires phoneme-level alignment
Regional accents (paulista vs nordestino) may affect confidence scores
Elision in casual speech needs robust fallback strategies

strengths: Mature ecosystem: Whisper, MFA, Kaldi all excellent for English
Strong research base for coarticulation modeling

technical_viability.vad_integration: GOOD - WebRTC VAD robust for multilingual content
technical_viability.real_time_potential: MODERATE - 2-3x audio length processing time expected

chosen_technique.primary_pipeline: Whisper → WhisperX Forced Alignment → WebRTC VAD → Viseme Mapping
rationale: WhisperX combines Whisper's multilingual ASR with wav2vec2 alignment precision
Supports both pt-BR and en-US out of the box with consistent API
Word and phoneme-level timestamps with confidence scores
Handles code-switching and accented speech well
chosen_technique.fallback_strategy: Energy-based segmentation with librosa for low-confidence regions

step_by_step.name: Audio Preprocessing
actions: Load audio with librosa, convert to mono 16kHz
Apply light denoising (spectral gating, -20dB threshold)
Normalize loudness to -23 LUFS (broadcast standard)
Trim silence from start/end (>500ms gaps)

step_by_step.name: Text Preprocessing
actions: Normalize punctuation (preserve diacritics for pt-BR)
Expand contractions: do→de o, na→em a, num→em um
Handle abbreviations: Sr.→Senhor, Dr.→Doutor
Create character mapping for animation system
pt_BR_specific: Map nh→ɲ, lh→ʎ for phoneme alignment

step_by_step.name: Initial ASR with Word Timestamps
actions: Run Whisper with word_timestamps=True
Language detection/validation against expected lang
Extract word-level start/end times and confidence
Filter words with confidence < min_confidence (0.5)

step_by_step.name: Forced Alignment Refinement
actions: Load WhisperX alignment model for target language
Align transcript to audio at phoneme/word granularity
Extract precise start/end boundaries with confidence scores
Handle alignment failures with fallback timing

granularity_options.phoneme: More precise, required for fast/casual pt-BR

step_by_step.name: Voice Activity Detection
actions: Run WebRTC VAD with 30ms frames, aggressiveness=2
Identify speech/non-speech segments
Merge consecutive non-speech >80ms into GAP tokens
Cross-validate with alignment boundaries

step_by_step.name: Token Merging & Gap Insertion
actions: Merge aligned words/phonemes with detected gaps
Insert GAP tokens for pauses >pause_min_ms
Resolve overlaps (prefer alignment over VAD timing)
Calculate final token durations and confidence scores

step_by_step.name: Phoneme-to-Viseme Mapping
actions: Apply language-specific phoneme→viseme conversion
Handle coarticulation with 20-40ms cross-fades
Map gaps to neutral/closed mouth position
Generate timeline events for animation system

step_by_step.name: Quality Validation
actions: Check timing drift: |sum(durations) - audio_length| ≤ 5ms
Validate coverage: aligned_tokens/total_tokens ≥ 95%
Confidence check: avg_confidence ≥ 0.7 for production use
Generate alignment visualization for manual review

text.description: Text content, empty string for gaps

python_minimal.core_function_description: Main alignment function using WhisperX + WebRTC VAD
key_steps: Load and preprocess audio to 16kHz mono
Run WhisperX transcription with word timestamps
Apply forced alignment for precise boundaries
Use WebRTC VAD to detect speech/non-speech regions
Merge aligned words with detected gaps
Return structured AlignmentResult with confidence scores
